    Orthogonality of the bricks T_Λ #

    Hom(T_Λ, T_Λ') = 0 when Λ \ Λ' is infinite (Bricks.hom_eq_zero). A morphism (g, h) is determined by γ = h(1, 0) ∈ k^(Λ'): for μ ∈ Λ \ Λ' the coordinates of g(e_μ) are γ_λ / (λ - μ), and the first component of b gives ∑_λ γ_λ / (λ - μ) = h(1, 0)₁ for all these μ. A rational function with simple poles that is constant at infinitely many points vanishes, so γ = 0 and then (g, h) = 0. In terms of P¹, Hom(O(D), O(D')) = H⁰(O(D' - D)) = 0 when D has infinitely many points outside D'.

    Ingredient of the Göbel–Simson construction (the rigid ω-families of their Proposition 3.5 are of this kind).

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.Bricks.rational_vanish {k : Type u} [Field k] (S : Finset k) (γ : k → k) (α : k) (M : Set k) (hM : M.Infinite) (hMS : ∀ μ ∈ M, μ ∉ S) (h : ∀ μ ∈ M, ∑ l ∈ S, γ l / (l - μ) = α) (l : k) :
    l ∈ S → γ l = 0

    A rational function ∑_{λ ∈ S} γ_λ / (λ - t) that equals a constant α at infinitely many points outside S vanishes, together with α.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.Bricks.hom_eq_zero {k : Type u} [Field k] {Λ Λ' : Set k} (hinf : (Λ \ Λ').Infinite) (f : T Λ ⟶ T Λ') :
    f = 0

    The bricks T_Λ and T_Λ' are orthogonal when Λ \ Λ' is infinite.
